task: Wing 3 — Zetrix AI: offshore-revenue / blockchain-revenue coincidence and customer identification
claim_under_investigation: The Edge Malaysia Weekly (14-20 Sep 2026): Zetrix's revenue from outside Malaysia equalled its blockchain/AI-related service revenue in 2024 (RM362.8m) and 2025 (RM643.5m); in 2023 overseas revenue RM127.6m vs blockchain/AI RM126.6m; no customer base or segmental detail beyond Malaysia/overseas split; quarterly token sales small vs total revenue.

coincidence_corroboration.verdict: PARTIALLY CORROBORATED (second outlet uses the identical figures for the blockchain/AI revenue line, confirming the two series are numerically identical in public reporting; but no source other than The Edge itself explicitly frames or explains the overseas=blockchain equality)
detail: The Malaysian Reserve, 'Zetrix's billion-ringgit profit paradox', 13 Oct 2026 (full text fetched, themalaysianreserve.com/2026-10-13/zetrixs-billion-ringgit-profit-paradox/): states 'Blockchain- and AI-related revenue increased from RM127.6 million in 2023 to RM362.8 million in 2024 and RM643.5 million in 2025.' These are EXACTLY the amounts The Edge attributes to BOTH overseas revenue and blockchain/AI revenue for 2024/2025 — independent confirmation that RM362.8m/RM643.5m are the blockchain/AI segment figures and that the same numbers circulate as the overseas-geography split.

Minor discrepancy worth noting: The Edge's 2023 pairing is RM127.6m overseas vs RM126.6m blockchain/AI (marginally lower); TMR instead lists RM127.6m as the 2023 blockchain/AI figure. One of the two attributions of the RM127.6m/RM126.6m pair is transposed in secondary coverage; the underlying pair of figures is the same.

No other outlet found that explicitly comments on the equality/identity of the offshore and blockchain revenue series. The framing 'revenue from outside the country is the same amount as blockchain/AI revenue' remains a single-source (The Edge) observation and editorial characterisation, even though the numbers themselves are double-sourced.

Contextual numbers from the TMR article (fetched): FY25 revenue RM1.34b (+31.3%), net profit RM883.85m (+24.9%); 1H26 normalised earnings +38.9% to RM540.7m 'supported by AI subscriptions and services, Web3 application fees and sales of Zetrix Layer-1 nodes'; MBSB Research estimated non-AI/non-blockchain activities still ~40% of group revenue.

found: MBSB Research (via The Malaysian Reserve, fetched): investors 'need to understand how much of the newer revenue is recurring, how much depends on individual transactions or technology sales, and how effectively it converts into cash' — closest thing to analyst commentary on the quality/composition of the blockchain/AI revenue; MBSB kept Buy (TP cut RM1.24→90sen on 26 Aug 2026), later placed rec/TP under review while FY26 core-earnings forecast RM1.1b unchanged.

MARC Ratings (via TMR, fetched): MARCWatch revised to Negative on 4 Oct 2026 citing 'heightened concerns about transparency and governance', saying it had NOT received sufficient information on the surge in borrowings and the allocation/utilisation of development expenditure; also cited the external auditor's resignation and payment arrears; warned it may suspend/withdraw the rating if information stays unavailable.

Auditor event: external auditor TGS TW PLT resigned; Zetrix attributed it to 'portfolio rationalisation and resource management'; TMR notes no evidence of a disagreement over accounting treatment. No auditor commentary on the revenue coincidence was found.

Structural red flags reported (TMR, fetched): cumulative development expenditure ~RM3.7b by end-June 2026 = 56% of total assets; borrowings RM2.19b (from RM160.5m in 2021); D&A +463.3% yoy in Q2; JPJ suspension over RM314m unremitted collections; market cap fell to ~RM600m vs projected RM1.1b earnings; Bursa UMA query after 50% intraday plunge (28 Aug 2026, FMT headline).
analyst_and_auditor_commentary.not_found: No analyst, auditor, regulator or forensic-accounting commentary that specifically addresses the offshore-revenue-equals-blockchain-revenue coincidence.

customer_identification.disclosure_status: Zetrix does not publicly disclose named customers or segmental detail beyond a Malaysia/overseas split; no customer-concentration disclosure was found in any accessible source (a Google News RSS query for 'Zetrix customer concentration' returned only an unrelated Web3Labs Nasdaq IPO item). The identified entities below come from partnership/deal announcements, NOT from revenue disclosures — their status as actual PAYING customers of the RM362.8m/RM643.5m revenue lines is unverified.

token_sales.corroboration: The Edge's characterisation that Zetrix sells tokens quarterly but the amounts are small vs total revenue is consistent with headline-level coverage found: 'Zetrix AI's earnings hit record high on blockchain fees and token sales' (The Edge, 27 Feb 2026) and '1Q profit jumps 49% on blockchain fees and node sales' (KLSE Screener, 25 May 2026). Revenue drivers publicly named: AI subscriptions/services, Web3 application fees, Zetrix Layer-1 node sales, token sales. No quantified token-sale figures were retrievable (paywalled).

Segment-level breakdown of the RM362.8m/RM643.5m into counterparties, or evidence of whether MBI, the Guangxi/China projects, or the Philippines MoU generated recognised revenue at those amounts. [UNVERIFIED] for all counterparty-to-revenue linkages.
assessment: The offshore-equals-blockchain coincidence is numerically double-sourced (The Edge + The Malaysian Reserve print identical RM362.8m/RM643.5m figures for blockchain/AI revenue), which strengthens the anomaly's factual basis while the 'same amount' framing itself stays single-source. Publicly-named counterparties are overwhelmingly state-linked: Guangxi state enterprise Beitou, Chinese national agencies (CAICT, Customs, Xinghuo network), Malaysia's MIMOS/MBI JV, and Philippine government bodies (DICT, BIR, NBI, SEC). That concentration pattern — opaque, government-linked, cross-border counterparties whose payments would by construction be 'overseas' revenue — makes the coincidental equality plausible as an artefact of how little is disaggregated, but no accessible source confirms actual payment flows, contract values, or recurrence. Third-party governance signals as of Oct 2026 are negative: MARCWatch Negative over transparency/information gaps, auditor resignation, RM314m unremitted JPJ collections, RM3.7b capitalised development spend (56% of assets), RM2.19b borrowings, and a 91.8% share-price drawdown.
